requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: The new metadata guard returns for every closed generic type, not just generic value types. Closed generic classes from referenced assemblies previously reached the closed-generic GetObjectInfo path without crashing; they now exit before collection, removing their formatter from the consuming compilation's generated output. This changes the explicitly required 'closed generic classes keep working as before' behaviour and can leave the consuming resolver unable to supply the previously generated Item<int> formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the repro library with `public partial class Item<T>` and a valid [Key(0)] property, then compile the app with Cmd.Member of type Item<int> and run MessagePackGenerator on base and head. Compare the generated formatter/resolver sources: base contains the collected Lib.Item<int> formatter and registration, while this guard on head bypasses that collection. The regression test should require the head output to retain the same Item<int> formatter and resolver registration as base.

hunches.claim: The new property-location helper also returns null for source-declared positional record properties, whose declaration syntax is a ParameterSyntax rather than a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For `[MessagePackObject] partial record R([property: Key(null)] string Value)`, `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` is therefore created with `Location.None` and then discarded by `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, silently losing the analyzer error for an invalid key even though the property is in the current compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.PositionalRecordNullKeyDiagnosticReceiptTests.NullKeyOnPositionalRecordPropertyIsStillDiagnosed. It analyzes a source positional record with `[property: Key(null)]` and requires a diagnostic whose ID is `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull.Id`; on head the helper supplies no source location and the new reporting filter drops it.

hunches.claim: The unkeyed-member regression test does not exercise the metadata-safe MemberNeedsKey diagnostic change. The new early return skips every metadata-defined generic type before member collection, so restoring the original DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing would leave all three new tests passing.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1083 remove-guard: item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() -> item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(); expected to survive because ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember and the other metadata generic cases return at the new DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty guard before reaching the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Skipping closed generic types with metadata-only original definitions means the consuming assembly does not analyze their members or generate a formatter for them; this matches the recorded product convention. The defining assembly owns those types, while the consuming assembly still generates its resolver for its own annotated types.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and receive no formatter from the compiling assembly; missing diagnostics or a formatter for such a type is not a defect. The new metadata-only guard and the accompanying README and MsgPack004 documentation implement that convention.
